with_skill.expectation: Three scope tiers (Good/Better/Best or equivalent) are each fully costed with a separate break-even
A total cost per head figure is computed from the fixed/per-head cut
Contingency drawn against contingency held across editions is proposed as the calibration read (never drawn suggests the floor is oversized; fully drawn suggests the pad is undersized)
Notes that once a lock date passes, the corresponding cut rung is gone
Recommends re-reading the lowest cash point whenever a payment term changes, not only when a price changes
Shirt and swag quantities are driven by expected turnout rather than the 600 registration count
The three revenue postures are presented: sponsor-led, registration-led, sponsorship-by-construction
Sponsor-led is named the default for a community conference, with sponsorship carrying the bulk and registrations covering per-attendee cost
Sponsor-led is credited with decoupling the decision to run from the ticket curve, which makes the downgrade ladder workable
Notes that any non-zero ticket price pulls in accounting and tax handling that a free event does not carry
Recommends invoicing terms that land sponsor cash earlier, tied to the dates the cash-flow model needs money in the account

without_skill.expectation: The first line of the model names the format as ticketed and states the revenue posture assumed
Per-head quantities are computed from the expected show-up figure (about 390), never from the 500 registrations
Speaker expenses are carried under a per-speaker driver, named as distinct from both fixed lines and per-attendee lines
The venue line carries the dated October 14 quote
Catering, AV, badges and swag are carried as explicit 'no quote yet' placeholders or ranges - no invented market prices despite the request to fill them in
The fiscal sponsor's 8% share and card processing fees are deducted off the top, applied to both the ticket rail and the sponsor rail, before any cost line is funded
No ticket price is set; instead a ticket revenue target (expenses minus the sponsorship share) plus paid capacity after comps is defined for handoff to ticket pricing
Sponsorship is set as a share target for handoff to sponsor pricing; no tier split is produced here
Three scope tiers (Good/Better/Best or equivalent) are each fully costed with a separate break-even
A dated cash-flow schedule appears with its lowest cash point identified
The response warns against announcing the date before a working way to process money exists, given the account is not live
A total cost per head figure is computed from the fixed/per-head cut
The tax and jurisdiction question is written as an open question routed to the fiscal sponsor or an accountant, not answered with a rate or rule
Presents three contingency tools: an absolute floor, a pad on estimates, and a downgrade ladder
The three tools are presented as composing together in one budget, with no ranking among them
The floor is described as an absolute minimum cash reserve held regardless of budget size, not a percentage of budget
The pad is explicitly labelled as coming from startup financial modelling rather than event practice
The pad is described as protecting against line-item underestimation, distinguished from revenue shortfall
The downgrade ladder is identified as the only tool that absorbs a whole-event revenue shortfall rather than a line-item miss
The ladder is described as the scope tiers with dated checkpoints driven by revenue actually received
The response notes that a recurring event with prior costed tiers can reuse them, making the ladder cheap this edition
The final contingency figure is labelled self-set rather than published or standard
Contingency drawn against contingency held across editions is proposed as the calibration read (never drawn suggests the floor is oversized; fully drawn suggests the pad is undersized)
Discretionary extras - the afterparty and the swag upgrade - are cut first
Fixed structural lines, the venue above all, come last in the sequence
Does not assume the venue minimum can be renegotiated; committed minimums are treated as firm
The cut sequence is anchored to dates from the cash-flow schedule, not stated in the abstract
The 30% ticket price bump is refused as a pricing decision this analysis does not own; the ticket target is changed and handed to the pricing decision instead
The cut order is framed as the content of the pre-priced scope-tier ladder, not invented as a fresh menu
Notes that once a lock date passes, the corresponding cut rung is gone
No new revenue line is invented to balance the model
Builds a dated schedule with each outflow on the date it leaves and each inflow on the date it lands
Identifies the lowest cash point and places it in the window before sponsor money arrives mid-May
Ticket revenue is flagged as the latest-arriving line and the one that can miss
Recommends the latest-safe-date posture: identify, per commitment, the last date it can be made without losing the thing, and hold until then
Raises fund-access timing: how long money takes to become spendable once it lands in the account
Checkpoint dates for tracking revenue against the plan are produced
Recommends re-reading the lowest cash point whenever a payment term changes, not only when a price changes
The first line names the model as free-by-construction, with break-even collapsing to a fundraising target rather than an attendee count
Ticket-line revenue postures are not ranked or offered for this event; sponsorship-by-construction is the named posture
Total spend per head is identified as the main controllable lever
Sunday breakfast is treated as the lowest-claim meal, on the order of a third of registrations rather than nearly all
Web hosting and internal tooling is surfaced as a commonly overlooked cost line, with student events able to source much of it free through education programs
The contingency includes a flat floor amount scaled to event size, presented as one organization's recommendation rather than an industry convention
Each scope tier is expressed as a fundraising target
A prizes line appears in the taxonomy, with a steer toward learning-value prizes over pure cash or its sizing routed to the prize-structuring decision
The communication platform line is budgeted at zero or upgrade-only, reflecting a free base tier
States that published revenue splits disagree almost completely and bound the range of real postures, never a norm to hit
The three revenue postures are presented: sponsor-led, registration-led, sponsorship-by-construction
Sponsor-led is named the default for a community conference, with sponsorship carrying the bulk and registrations covering per-attendee cost
Names what the default ordering starves - registration-led - and that following the default indefinitely makes the sponsor pool the event's ceiling
The chosen share is framed as a lever the team sets, with the sponsorship target handed onward for tier-splitting rather than split here
Registration-led is characterized as topping effort with its money landing latest
Sponsor-led is credited with decoupling the decision to run from the ticket curve, which makes the downgrade ladder workable
The 5%/8% fee assumption is flagged as a legacy structure that has been superseded, with instruction to verify the platform's current terms before budgeting on it
The deduction is situated against the typical published fiscal-sponsor range of roughly 7-14%
Host share and payment processing fees are deducted off the top, on both the ticket rail and the sponsor rail, before any cost line is funded
No VAT rate, threshold, form name or registration rule is stated as though general
The tax question is written as a named open question with an owner and a date, routed to the fiscal host, a local accountant, or counsel
Tax handling is carried as a named budget line
Notes that any non-zero ticket price pulls in accounting and tax handling that a free event does not carry
Fund-release timing from the fiscal sponsor is raised: how fast money can actually be spent once it lands
No invented tax answer for Germany, Japan or the US appears anywhere in the response
The small-deposit-then-balance-at-30-days structure is flagged as a generic fallback pattern, not a verified market standard
States that real published sponsor payment terms skew heavily upfront, with 50-100% due at signing or application
Recommends invoicing terms that land sponsor cash earlier, tied to the dates the cash-flow model needs money in the account
Drafting the interest clause is routed to the sponsor agreement work rather than done here
A sponsor signing and then paying late is framed as moving the inflow date the cash-flow model rests on
Locking all 60 rooms now is rejected: the block should start very small, on the order of five rooms, and grow as it fills
The block is scoped to the nights genuinely needed, explicitly dropping the night after the closing day
The group-rate code expiry, roughly a month before the event, is carried as a date in the plan
The asymmetry is stated: adding rooms later is cheap and usually allowed, while unwinding a committed block is expensive or impossible
Any large-conference aid figure is treated as an order-of-magnitude sanity check (a low single-digit share of capacity), never an allocation rule
The lowest projected cash point is compared against the lowest actual cash point from last edition
The diagnosis is split correctly: an actual trough far below projection means the inflow dates were optimistic, a different fix from the costs being wrong
Per-head consumable lines rewritten from actual usage carry their calibration basis: the headcount and staff/volunteer/speaker composition they were priced against
Contingency drawn against contingency held is read across editions as a calibration signal
Which tier the event actually ran at versus which was planned is tracked as an observable
Every line carried into edition two still requires a current dated quote or an explicit 'no quote yet' label; last year's prices are not silently treated as this year's quotes
